summary: Deer Point Light: a small round white tower at the southern tip of Deer Island, New Brunswick, beside the Old Sow whirlpool. It never had a keeper.

structures.note: LighthouseFriends 6.1 m (20 ft); Lighthouse Directory 6 m (20 ft); CCG list: white cylindrical tower. Record gives 6.0 m. Build date not found.

access.note: In Deer Island Point Park, reached by road with parking. Grounds open, tower closed (LighthouseFriends; Lighthouse Directory).

corrections.why: LighthouseFriends says the light is known officially as Deer Point Light. The CCG list of lights and Rowlett both give Deer Point. The record's name repeats the island in a way the official name does not. For human review; a disambiguating island name can stay in the display name if wanted.

notes_for_editor: Thin station. No build or first-lighting date found in any source: LighthouseFriends and the CCG list give none, Rowlett says 'Date unknown', the corpus Marine reports (which run to fiscal 1923-24) do not mention Deer Point, and a web search for its history returned nothing. The story says the sources do not date it, and gives no reason for its construction. Characteristic: LighthouseFriends and the CCG list give LFl R 12s (2 s flash in a 12 s period); Rowlett gives 2 s on, 8 s off (a 10 s period). Not reconciled. Focal height 9.6 m (CCG) against a 10 m focal plane (Rowlett). Name: the record's name, LighthouseFriends' page title 'Deer Island Point Lighthouse', the CCG list and Rowlett 'Deer Point', and LighthouseFriends' 'Known officially as Deer Point Light' all differ; see the proposed correction. kind: LighthouseFriends says the light does not merit inclusion on an official lighthouse list and has no lantern room; the record's kind 'lighthouse' is left for a human to review. Not used: the Cyberlights page (a 2000 visit; copyrighted, not quoted); the Wikipedia Old Sow article (lead only; not read in full); Lorimer's 1876 book (read only as quoted by Backyard History); US Coast Guard and Seamagazine pages on 'Deer Island Light', which are a different light at Lubec, Maine. Biggest gap for a future pass: the Canadian Coast Guard's aids-to-navigation records, or a Canadian Coast Guard or Parks history of Deer Island Point, if one exists.
